Subject: Ephemeral cross-region egress for debug: audit & DPA questions

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To summarize your ask: HealthMetrics needs a narrowly scoped, timeboxed ability for our support/infra team to perform live debugging and telemetry replay that will briefly move a subset of logs and anonymized traces from the EU tenant to a US debug cluster (no PII, tokenized telemetry only). You asked for operational guardrails we can sign off on and what evidence you’ll get for audits.

Quick proposal from our side:
- Scope: tokenized analytics & trimmed traces only (no user message content, no embeddings).
- Window: default 4-hour canary window; escalation to 48h with written approval.
- Controls: KMS-wrapped transfer, per-transfer audit log (immutable), dedicated subprocessor roster for debug path.
- Telemetry retention: audit logs retained 90 days; payload artifacts removed immediately after verification.

I attached a short playbook (ephemeral-egress-playbook.pdf) and our current debug subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_20270402.csv). Can you confirm whether HealthMetrics legal needs a DPA addendum or a short operational attestation will suffice for your compliance review?

Next steps: if this shape is acceptable we can draft an addendum and a 1-page attestation for your security team to sign.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: Ephemeral cross-region egress for debug: audit & DPA questions

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from our side:
1) Can you confirm the exact processors on the debug path (SaaS vendors we’ll see in the chain)? We need vendor names and countries for our Data Processing Addendum review.
2) Is the KMS wrapping customer-managed or Redwood-managed? For our regulated workloads we prefer customer-managed keys where feasible.
3) Will the audit logs include per-request identifiers that we can correlate to our own telemetry? We need traceability for incident reconstructions.

Legal will review the attachments but they generally prefer an addendum to the DPA for any cross-border processing even if timeboxed. If you can provide a short attestation + the vendor list (with countries), that will speed review.

Thanks —
Sam
Sam Park
Senior Security Architect, HealthMetrics
sam.park@healthmetrics.com

Sam / Naomi —

Quick answers from ops & security engineering:
- Subprocessors on the ephemeral debug path: GCP Logging (us-central1), Sentry (us-east-1), Datadog (EU/US hybrid — logs forwarded to US staging). Full roster attached (CSV).
- KMS: we can offer two modes: (A) Redwood-managed CMKs with customer-specific key isolation (default); (B) Customer-managed key (bring-your-own-key) via our KMS integration, but that adds ~2 business days for key provisioning and test.
- Audit logs: yes — they contain immutable request IDs, sender principal, timestamp, transfer bytes, and transfer purpose tag. We’ll provide a signed hash snapshot of the log after each window for your audit.

Operational constraints we’d surface: the debug cluster will not run model scoring on raw customer messages — only pre-filtered, tokenized telemetry. Network egress uses a dedicated ephemeral route and is disabled automatically at window end.

If HealthMetrics legal wants an addendum, we can generate a short DPA annex that limits cross-border processing to the described debug windows and excludes content/embeddings.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Sam —

Thanks for the quick review and the questions. Action plan:
1) I’ll loop in Legal to prepare a concise DPA annex that limits cross-border processing to tokenized telemetry, sets the default canary to 4 hours, and requires written elevation for anything beyond 48 hours. (DocuSign link to follow.)
2) Kimberly will stand up a test transfer with a masked sample payload and produce the signed log-hash for HealthMetrics to validate traceability.
3) If you want CMK control, let us know and we’ll provision the BYOK workflow; otherwise we’ll proceed with isolated Redwood-managed CMKs to avoid key-provisioning delays.

Proposed next step for speed: sign the operational attestation so ops can run a single 4-hour canary next week. I included the Drive link to the playbook and HubSpot deal for the addendum tracking.

If legal confirms they want the addendum I’ll ask our contracts team to route the short annex for review.
